title: Measuring the Operation, Not the Name: a protocol for asking whether a corpus's stylistic structure follows its author-names, with the controls that make the answer mean something (v0.4, with reference implementation)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Computational authorship attribution normally asks which of several candidates wrote a text, presupposing that the candidates are authors and that the corpus divides among them. This protocol specifies the prior question — does a corpus's stylistic structure follow its author-names at all? — and the controls without which any answer is worthless. The instrument is deliberately ordinary (short-word, character-trigram and morphological-ending profiles on fixed blocks; unsupervised PC1 and k-means; leave-one-TEXT-out nearest-centroid with vocabulary and scaling fitted inside each fold). What is not ordinary is the requirement: a bounded single-author control; distinct authors sharing a genre; a documented attribution projected out of sample; blind labels from a second reader; and a text-level label-permutation null in place of a majority baseline, because a nearest-centroid classifier will separate almost any partition of any corpus. Two referee rounds are recorded in the paper with their corrections applied and two of the author's own claims withdrawn: that the Aristotle/Theophrastus names sit at chance (false — supervised attribution recovers them at 0.798 balanced, outside the null), and that an assumed authorial voice cannot split from its own author (false — Chatterton's Rowley forgery separates from his acknowledged verse at 0.864, numerically similar to three genuinely distinct tragedians at 0.872). The surviving claims are comparative and stated with their dependencies: operation partitions the corpus better than the names on identical folds (0.860 vs 0.798, with a null for the difference itself and a bootstrap CI that leaves the ordering descriptive); name recovery falls to 0.564 when botanical and zoological works are removed, which a 120-draw matched-removal test places in the lower 15% of equivalent removals — suggestive of subject dependence, not a demonstration of it. The protocol's hardest limit, stated as its own finding: no supervised separation, however strong, licenses an inference to distinct makers, in either direction. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. Written and computed in-session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) at MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction; the requirement of a documented-forgery ground truth before circulation, and the principle that an authorship determination is not arrived at by a mere mean, are Lee Sharks's; two referee rounds by a second reader (ChatGPT, 2026-09-07) produced the corrections recorded in §5c, adopted on their terms, including the withdrawal of two of the author's claims. The protocol and its errors are Lee Sharks's.

wiki_article: "Measuring the Operation, Not the Name" is a methodological protocol by Lee Sharks (v0.4, 7 September 2026) for the question prior to authorship attribution: whether a corpus's stylistic structure follows its author-names at all. Its instrument is ordinary — short-word, trigram and ending profiles on fixed blocks, unsupervised PC1 and k-means, leave-one-text-out nearest-centroid with vocabulary and scaling fitted inside each fold — and its substance is the control series: a bounded single-author corpus, distinct authors sharing a genre, a documented attribution projected out of sample, blind labels from a second reader, and a text-level permutation null in place of a majority baseline, because a nearest-centroid classifier will separate almost any partition of any corpus. Two referee rounds are recorded with their corrections applied and two of the author's own claims withdrawn: that the Aristotle/Theophrastus names sit at chance, and that an assumed authorial voice cannot split from its own author — Chatterton's Rowley forgery separates from his acknowledged verse at 0.864, numerically similar to three distinct tragedians at 0.872. The protocol's hardest limit follows from that and is stated as its own finding: no supervised separation, however strong, licenses an inference to distinct makers, in either direction. The surviving claims are comparative and carry their dependencies. A CC0 reference implementation is included in the body and as an attachment.

defines_concepts.definition: The four runs a partition claim must be bracketed by before it is evidence: a bounded single-author corpus, distinct authors sharing a genre, a documented attribution projected out of sample, and the target — with blind labels added whenever the labels are the analyst's own.

The protocol's hardest limit, measured rather than cautioned: a documented single hand writing in a sustained assumed voice separates from itself at the magnitude at which distinct authors separate, so no supervised separation licenses an inference to distinct makers.

falsification_conditions: The protocol fails if its controls do not behave as reported when rerun from the named open sources; if the permutation nulls are not reproduced; if the matched-removal distribution differs materially; or if a case is exhibited where the control series licenses a partition claim that independent evidence contradicts. The paper's own withdrawn claims are recorded rather than removed so that the corrections are inspectable.
methodology: Three feature families reported together; fixed-size blocks; unsupervised and supervised procedures kept apart and both reported for target and controls; vocabulary and scaling fitted inside each fold; text-level label permutation as the comparator; matched removals before attributing a drop to what was removed; blind labels when the labels are the analyst's; every file verified by its opening words.
